2. The Suit in O.S. No.414/2020 had been filed by respondent No.1 seeking for the following reliefs:
a) To pass a Judgement and Decree against the defendant for permanent injunction restraining the defendants without due course of law, their agents, servants,
subordinates and henchmen in interfering with peaceful Possession and enjoyment in respect of the plaint schedule property.
b) To pass such other relief/s as the Hon'ble Court may deem fit to grant under the circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and equity.

SCHEDULE All that piece and parcel of the property land bearing Sy.No.37/P11, Measuring 2 Acre 20 Guntas, Situated at Haralluru Village, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural Dist and bounded on East by : Land belongs to Mr.Pillappa;

sentences.text: The land having been acquired, the plaintiff would have no subsisting right, title or interest in the said property, let alone seek for an order of injunction.

The said application having been opposed, the trial Court vide the impugned order dated 31.10.2023 dismissed the said application on the ground that the consideration of an application under Order 7 Rule 11 has to be made only on the basis of the averments made in the plaint and most of the submissions made under Order 7 Rule 11 application is in the nature of defence raised by the defendant which cannot be considered insofar as an application under Order 7 Rule 11 is concerned.
5. Sri.
Prasanna.

V.R, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in para 8 of the plaint, the plaintiff has categorically admitted that acquisition proceedings have been completed and it is contended by the plaintiff himself that due to the acquisition proceedings being completed,
defendant No.1 cannot interfere with the possession of the plaintiff.

This very statement was sufficient for the trial Court to have taken into consideration for rejection of the plaint on an application being filed NC: 2024:KHC:21179 under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC since once acquisition is completed, the plaintiff would have no right, title or interest in the property.
This submission of Sri.Prasanna.V.R, is supported by Sri.P.V.Chandrashekhar, learned counsel for respondent No.1-KIADB.

He reiterates the reference to both para 8 of the plaint as also submits that acquisition proceedings have been completed the KIADB has taken possession and the plaintiff is not in possession of the property to maintain a suit for bare injunction.

6. Plaintiff/respondent No.1 though has entered appearance by way of caveat through a counsel,
none has been appearing for respondent No.1.

7. Having heard the counsel for the petitioner and counsel for the respondents and having perused the papers, I am of the considered opinion that the plaint itself indicates that there is an acquisition proceeding which has been completed.
Once the acquisition proceeding is completed, the plaintiff herein would NC: 2024:KHC:21179 not have any subsisting right, title or interest in the property.

Insofar as the contention that the plaintiff is in possession, the plaintiff has not sought for any relief against KIADB or State of Karnataka, suitable remedy would be for such person to challenge the acquisition notification in a writ court as provided under law, a suit not being maintainable and suit being barred in respect of any such properties.

8. Such being the case, there being no challenge to the acquisition made, the suit being barred as regards the lands which had been acquired by the State for and on behalf of KIADB, the said averment in para 8 ought to have been properly construed by the trial Court and the plaint was required to be rejected on that ground.
This aspect not having been properly considered by the trial Court, I am of the considered opinion that the impugned order is required to be set-aside.
